what: Every declared kernel that NEITHER emitter places. This is the tile-rs acceptance backlog: the point of keeping it is that a kernel the AscendC and PTO paths both refuse should still be a target the lift can take, rather than being dropped from the inventory. `rust/tests/test_tile_rs_acceptance.py` keeps this in step with the manifests, so a kernel that starts placing must leave the file. Each entry also records `needs`: the mechanism that would place it. A backlog without that is a list of complaints. One correction: an earlier version of this file said rspto had no chunked path. It has one for blocked matmul; the gap is that it does not generalise to an elementwise chain.

deepseek_v41/argmax_v41_8x129280.ascendc: mlir_to_cpp: __tile_argmax_f32 over 8 rows -- the scan carries a single running index, so only one row is expressible; emit one call per row.
deepseek_v41/argmax_v41_8x129280.needs: a PTO arm and a generator section; this row is hand-captured

deepseek_v41/argmax_v41_8x131072_pad.pto: NPU UB budget (arch a2a3): tile of 65536B at offset 131584B would use 197120B > UB_SIZE 194560B (C1)
deepseek_v41/argmax_v41_8x131072_pad.ascendc: mlir_to_cpp: __tile_argmax_f32 over 8 rows -- the scan carries a single running index, so only one row is expressible; emit one call per row.
deepseek_v41/argmax_v41_8x131072_pad.needs: the chunked path GENERALISED in rspto. It is not chunk-less -- the blocked-matmul path already emits `scf.for` over N-blocks with a dynamic `%n_off` in its partition_view (mlir_to_pto.rs:752-775) -- but that machinery is specific to the cube/tpop path and does not reach an elementwise chain. What is missing is the generalisation, plus, ONLY for a width with no 32-byte-aligned divisor, an epilogue for the tail -- `plan_chunks` now prefers an exact divisor so the loop is uniform and a static-shape tile can be reused
